settings.point_estimate: mean over the 5 repeat-level pooled out-of-fold metrics

integrity_checks_passed: folds CSV: 25 valid folds (non-null accuracy), unique split indices, repeat/fold consistent, scenario correct
predictions: no duplicate (split, patient); per fold the record count equals n_val and the Dies count equals n_dies_val
every patient exactly once per repeat; same patients and classes in every repeat and in both scenarios
pooled accuracy and pooled recall(Dies) of every repeat reproduce the fold-size-weighted CSV values to 1e-9
limitations: The independent units are the 165 patients (63 Dies, 102 Lives). The 5 repeats re-train models on heavily overlapping data and re-predict the same patients; averaging over repeats reduces training randomness but does not add patients.

The bootstrap resamples PATIENTS and keeps each repeat's trained models fixed. The interval therefore reflects patient (case-mix) sampling uncertainty only; it does not include variability from re-training on different training sets. The SD over the 5 repeat values describes that variation descriptively only (the 5 repeats are not independent).

No hypothesis test and no p-value is computed. An interval that excludes zero is not, by itself, evidence of superiority: four metrics are reported, the direction of the fold-level means was seen before this analysis, and the comparison must be described as exploratory unless it was pre-specified.

Pooled per-repeat metrics use all 165 out-of-fold predictions of a repeat (each from one of 5 different fold models), so they differ from the fold-level means in the folds CSV. Accuracy and recall(Dies) are reconciled against the CSV exactly; MCC and recall(Lives) are not stored there and cannot be reconciled.
The decision threshold is the pipeline's own 0.5. Only the scenarios 'none' and 'ctgan' exist in Phase 3 (SMOTE variants were evaluated only in Phase 2).
